sections.h2: What kind of city is Bowling Green, Kentucky, for a home seller?
sections.html:
Bowling Green is a college-and-factory city of 78,505 people by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up 8.6 percent from the 2020 base. It is the seat of Warren County, sits on the Barren River and ranks third in Kentucky behind Louisville and Lexington. The city covers about 40 square miles of land. Interstate 65 runs through it between Louisville and Nashville, Interstate 165 heads north to Owensboro, and US 31W, US 231 and US 68/KY 80 cross town as well.

One number frames the local housing market: only 36.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, according to the 2020 to 2024 Census figures. That is a renter's city, so a house here is often sold to an investor or landlord as readily as to a family.

sections.h2: How did Bowling Green grow into its present housing stock?
sections.html:
Settlers carved their names into beech trees near the river around 1775, and the town took shape from homesteads of the Moore family and General Elijah Covington. County commissioners met in 1798 and named the place "Bolin Green." The Louisville and Nashville Railroad arrived in 1859. In November 1861 Confederate Kentuckians made the city their provisional capital, and the occupiers withdrew in February 1862 after burning the depot and the bridges over the Barren River.

Growth after 1950 was steady: the city counted 18,347 people that year, 40,641 in 1990, 58,067 in 2010 and 72,294 in 2020. That is growth of about 78 percent since 1990, so the stock mixes downtown storefronts from the 1870s with subdivisions from the last three decades.

sections.h2: What drives jobs and demand for houses in Bowling Green?
sections.html:
Western Kentucky University is the biggest employer, with 3,274 people on the payroll in the city's 2022 financial report. A 2011 study put WKU salaries at roughly a tenth of all income earned in Warren County. A short list of other anchors follows.

  • General Motors' Bowling Green Assembly Plant has built every Chevrolet Corvette since 1981 and employed about 1,100 people as of 2022. The National Corvette Museum is also in town.
  • Fruit of the Loom, headquartered here, employed about 930 in 2022.
  • Holley Performance Products has made parts in the city since 1952 and been headquartered here since 1994.
  • Kobe Steel opened an aluminum assembly plant in 2018.
  • AESC announced a battery plant in 2022 expected to be fully operating in 2027, and AKFA Aluminum began building a plant in May 2026 that is projected to create 331 jobs.

Houchens Industries, one of the country's largest employee-owned companies, is based in Bowling Green.

sections.h2: Who lives in Bowling Green, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
The city is younger and lower-income than Kentucky as a whole. The median resident was 29.5 in the 2020 census, 15.0 percent of residents are foreign-born and 22.1 percent speak a language other than English at home. The median household earns $48,873, and 25.6 percent of residents live in poverty.

  • Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $241,900.
  • Median gross rent is $998 a month.
  • Median owner costs are $1,447 with a mortgage and $553 without.
  • The 2020 census counted 31,797 housing units, with 11.4 percent vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 11.5 percent.
  • Households total 30,633 and the average household has 2.28 people.

With rental vacancy above 11 percent, a house listed as a rental can sit empty between leases, which is worth weighing if you own one.

sections.h2: Which school district is a Bowling Green house in?
sections.html:
It depends on the address. The Bowling Green Independent School District serves the inner part of the city, and Warren County Public Schools covers the outlying sections. The city's own finance page describes an "annex" of homes inside city limits that attend county schools, and the school tax rate differs between the two.

The independent district's elementary schools are Dishman-McGinnis, Parker Bennett Curry, Potter Gray, T.C. Cherry and W.R. McNeill. Bowling Green High and the Carol Martin Gatton Academy of Mathematics and Science also belong to that district. Warren County Public Schools operates the rest of the area's schools, including Drakes Creek, Henry F. Moss, Warren East and South Warren middle schools. Tell buyers which district applies, since it moves the tax figure.

sections.h2: How are Bowling Green property tax rates set by location?
sections.html:
The city's Treasury office collects tax for the city itself and for the Bowling Green Independent School System, while the Warren County Sheriff collects the county bill. The city mails roughly 23,000 bills each October, due in full by December 31. Its finance page warns that unpaid city taxes can face a foreclosure action filed six months after the due date. The rates below are per $100, as the city lists them.

Real estate tax rates per $100 by location, City of Bowling Green Finance Department
Where the house isTotal real estate rate
City proper (city limits and city schools)1.3625
Annex (city limits, county schools)1.0455
Outside city limits (county schools)0.8425

City proper adds a 0.2030 city rate and an 0.8420 city school rate to the county's 0.2145 and the state's 0.1030. Check the Finance page for the rate in force when you sell.

sections.h2: How do I pay the county bill, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
The Warren County Sheriff prefers a check or money order mailed to P.O. Box 807, Bowling Green, KY 42102, or delivered to 1347 KY-185, Suite 1. The office answers at (270) 842-1633. Online card payments carry a $1.50 fee up to $60 and 2.49 percent above that. Partial payments are not accepted on a current-year bill.

  • 2 percent discount from October 1 through November 1, face value from November 2 through December 31, a 5 percent penalty in January and 21 percent from February 1 through April 15.
  • Kentucky law issues the bill in the name of the January 1 owner. If you sold, forward the bill to the buyer.
  • A closing agent or attorney usually prorates the year between buyer and seller, but the sheriff needs the full bill paid by one or both of them.

For a delinquent prior year, call the Warren County Clerk at (270) 842-9416 for the payoff. The PVA at (270) 843-3268 handles the homestead and disability exemptions for owners 65 or older or totally disabled.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Bowling Green tax bills?
sections.html: After April 15 an unpaid bill becomes a certificate of delinquency, recorded as a lien under KRS 134.122, and the County Attorney reports 12 percent annual interest under KRS 134.125. If the certificate stays unpaid 90 days, third-party purchasers may buy it. The 2026 clerk's sale was held on August 26 at 9 am at 429 E 10th Ave, Suite 100. A certificate cannot be sold while the owner has a payment agreement with the County Attorney, whose office offers plans running 4 to 8 months at (270) 782-2760. If a purchaser already bought the certificate, you deal with that purchaser instead.

sections.h2: Which city permits touch a Bowling Green house sale?
sections.html:
The Building and Inspection Division at 707 E Main Ave, reachable at 270-393-3615 or 270-393-3676 on weekdays from 8 am to 4 pm, issues permits. A building permit is required to construct, enlarge, alter, repair or demolish, or to change a building's use. The fee is $20 up to $3,000 of work, then $2.50 per $1,000 above that up to $500,000. All fences need a permit, and an accessory structure under 200 square feet falls under a no-fee permit. A certificate of occupancy costs $3 after a final inspection.

Converting a house to a short-term rental counts as a change of use. It needs inspections and a $45 Short Term Rental Permit. If you are selling a house that someone else operates that way, ask for the permit paperwork.

faqs.q: What is the current population of Bowling Green, KY?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 78,505 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 72,294 counted in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Bowling Green?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $241,900 for 2020 to 2024. Only 36.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Is Bowling Green property tax higher inside the city?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists a total real estate rate of 1.3625 per $100 for city proper, 1.0455 for the annex and 0.8425 outside city limits.

faqs.q: Which office handles a delinquent Bowling Green tax bill?
faqs.a: The Warren County Clerk, at (270) 842-9416, for a payoff. The County Attorney at (270) 782-2760 sets up payment plans.

faqs.q: Is a city permit required to list a Bowling Green house?
faqs.a: No permit is needed to sell, but the city requires them for building work and for converting a house to a short-term rental. Close out any open permit work before you list.
